For Petitioner : Mr.Sulthan Basha  for M/s.Ajmal Associates For Respondent : Mrs.S.Prabha   Government Advocate  :ORDER  This petition challenges the proceedings in case pending trial in C.C.No.59 of 2006 on the file of Judicial Magistrate No.II, Nagercoil.
2.Petitioner is the third accused in the case.
He and two others are facing prosecution for offences under Section 16(1)(a)(1) and (ii) r/w 7(1) & 2(19)(a)(b) & (m) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 55 of PPA Rules, 1955.

sentences.text: 3.The petitioner is a general merchant engaged inter-alia in sale of coriander.
It is alleged that samples seized from the petitioner's shop was found adulterated by mixing of sulphur-dioxide with coriander powder.

4.Learned counsel for petitioner submits that though the report of the Public Analyst, Chennai,
dated 28.10.2005 informed of the sample containing sulphur-dioxide, the complaint had been preferred by the respondent only on 27.06.2006.
Notice under Section 13(2) of the Act informing the right of the petitioner to seek analysis of the second sample had been issued only on 28.06.2006.

The right of the petitioner/accused to have a second analysis of the sample seized had been rendered nugatory by the fact that the very complaint as also the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act had been issued much after the expiry of the shelf life of the product.

In support of such submission,
learned counsel relied on the judgment of the Apex Court in Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah v C.C.Jani and another [JT 2009 (12) SC80].

entities.text: Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah v C.C.Jani and another [JT 2009 (12) SC80]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph No.8 of such judgment reads as follows:
"8.

It will be apparent from the above, that only on receipt of the report of the Public Analyst under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, can a prosecution be launched and a copy of the report could be supplied to the accused.

Sub-section (2) also indicates that on receipt of the report the accused could, if he so desired, make an application to the court within a period of 10 days from the date of the receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.

In other words, in the instant case, the appellant was prevented from applying for analysis of the second sample before 17th July, 1989, by which time the second sample of curd had deteriorated and was not capable of being analysed as was found in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [1967 (2) SCR 116].

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [1967 (2) SCR 116]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5.Learned Government Advocate (Crl.side) submits that after due inspection and seizing of samples in keeping with the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, it had been found that the product sold by the petitioner/accused contained sulphur-dioxide.
He would contend that a prima facie case stood made out against the petitioner and he would have to establish his innocence in the course of trial.

6.This petition would succeed on the ground that the public analysis report on the sample seized from the petitioner was obtained on 24.09.2005, the private complaint in the case was preferred on 27.06.2006 and notice under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act was issued only on 28.06.2006.

In Ghisa Ram's case, the Apex Court has held that where opportunity to have the second sample analysed by the Central Food Laboratory was afforded to the accused after much delay, by which time the second sample would have deteriorated, such right would be rendered nugatory.
Such reasoning would apply on all fours in the instant case.
7.Accordingly, these Criminal Original Petitions stand allowed and the proceedings in C.C.No.59 of 2006 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate II, Nagercoil, shall stand quashed.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
